ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: on the left side of the figure is a benzene ring, and it shares one fused C-C edge with the oxygen-containing heterocycle on the right; above the right heterocycle there is an ether oxygen, at the upper right there is a carbonyl C=O, the right-side carbon is connected to R and H, and the bottom carbon is connected to OH and an unlabeled carbon substituent. Arrows and unbonded :B are also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: count by blocks according to the specified method. The benzene ring has a total of 6 independent C-C bonds, and the shared fused vertical bond is counted only once. The right heterocycle, apart from the shared fused bond, also includes aryl C-O, O-carbonyl carbon, carbonyl carbon-alpha C, alpha C-bottom C, bottom C-aryl C, altogether 5. The carbonyl C=O is treated as 1 bond. Heavy-atom substituent bonds include alpha C-R 1 bond, bottom C-unlabeled carbon substituent 1 bond, and the C-O in bottom C-OH 1 bond, altogether 3. Exclude alpha C-H and O-H bonds, and ignore all arrows and unbonded :B. Therefore the total is 6 + 5 + 1 + 3 = 15.

method.method_draft: Partition the structure into pieces. Count the benzene ring as 6 unique C-C bonds, including the fused vertical bond only once. Then count the additional bonds making the right-hand heterocycle beyond the shared fused bond: aryl C-O, O-carbonyl C, carbonyl C-alpha C, alpha C-bottom C, and bottom C-aryl C = 5. Add the carbonyl C=O as 1 bond. Add heavy-atom substituent bonds: alpha C-R = 1, bottom C-unlabeled carbon substituent = 1, and bottom C-O of the OH group = 1. Exclude the alpha C-H and the O-H part of OH, and ignore all arrows and the unbonded :B. Sum 6 + 5 + 1 + 3 = 15.
